rationale: B wins because it gives the founder more real lanes without pretending they are all launch-day pitches. A's "Wise routes cross-border business payments through a regulated stablecoin, skipping correspondent banks" is a strong payments-infrastructure shape, but it leads with an overclaim it later admits it cannot yet prove. B's "Investors will ask what stablecoin settlement does to Wise's margins" adds the listed-company economics lane A missed, and "Treat it as a second-wave story, not a launch-day pitch" is the kind of adult supervision these exercises usually lack.
gaps_in_A: "skipping correspondent banks" overstates the mechanism before the update proves which banking leg, if any, the stablecoin replaces.
"the trend a market's edge case becomes its plumbing" tries to make a category shift out of one launch; A does ask for comparable evidence, but the headline is still doing victory-lap work too early.
"Wise's stablecoin rolls out market by market — a map of where the regulators say yes" needs the actual market list and approvals; without them, it is a regulatory thesis, not a story.
A misses two useful lanes B catches: listed-company margin impact and a second-wave customer treasury story.
gaps_in_B: "turns its launch sequence into a public map" runs ahead of the facts; the update says rollout is region by region but gives no first market, approval list, or blocked markets.
"direct challenge to those banks' revenue line" is a fair newsroom question, but the update gives no bank revenue exposure or evidence of displacement.
"the first analyst questions will land in the next reporting cycle" is plausible, not sourced. Do not dress calendar speculation as a peg.
"Why a business would hold a stablecoin balance to pay suppliers abroad" is useful but unready; B correctly says it cannot run until there is a named customer, corridor, amount, and savings.
